title: Tonkatsu
subtitle: Japanese breaded and deep-fried pork cutlet
excerpt: The great Japanese fried pork dish: a thick pork loin cutlet coated in panko breadcrumbs and deep-fried until deeply golden and crisp, served sliced with shredded cabbage and a glossy tonkatsu sauce. Remarkably simple and consistently excellent.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tonkatsu (from the Japanese pronunciation of pork and the German Schnitzel, Katsu) was developed in Japan in the late nineteenth century as part of the yoshoku tradition of adapting Western dishes to Japanese palates. The use of panko breadcrumbs rather than regular breadcrumbs is essential: panko is made from bread without crusts, processed to create large, airy flakes that absorb less oil and produce a dramatically crispier crust. The thick pork loin cut (at least 2 to 3 cm) distinguishes tonkatsu from other fried pork dishes and ensures the meat stays juicy during the high-heat frying. Tonkatsu sauce is typically a fruit-based Worcestershire-style sauce; Bulldog is the most famous brand.

recipeTools.notes: A deep, heavy pan for frying.

content.text: The oil temperature must be 170 to 175 C and maintained throughout: too hot and the panko burns before the pork cooks through; too cool and the crust absorbs oil and becomes greasy. Test with a breadcrumb: it should sizzle immediately and float. Fry in batches rather than crowding the pan. Rest on a rack, not kitchen paper, to prevent steam softening the crust.

items.preparation: chops about 2.5 cm thick, bone removed; at room temperature
for deep-frying; at least 7 cm deep in the pan
mixed with 2 tbsp ketchup for tonkatsu sauce

content.text: Cut 3 to 4 shallow slits through the fat and connective tissue on the edge of each pork chop to prevent curling during frying. Season the pork on both sides with salt and pepper. Set up a breading station: flour, beaten egg, and panko in three separate shallow dishes.

Coat each cutlet in flour, shaking off excess, then dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko on both sides so the crumbs adhere completely. Heat the oil to 170 to 175 C in a deep, heavy pan. Fry the cutlets for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden. They should be cooked through (70 C internal). Drain on a rack for 2 minutes.
Slice the tonkatsu diagonally into 3 cm strips. Serve on a bed of shredded raw cabbage with the tonkatsu sauce drizzled over or served alongside. Eaten with a bowl of rice and miso soup.
